preview: An interview experience for the Technical Sales Associate (TSA) Intern role at Texas Instruments, detailing the online assessment, two rigorous interview rounds involving technical, sales, and behavioral questions, and helpful tips.
content: TEXAS INSTRUMENTS Experience Role: Technical Sales Associate (TSA) Intern ARYAN SANJAY SHAH BTech Electronics Engineering 2021 - 2025 Eligibility Criteria CGPA - 6.00 + Branches - EXTC, Electronics, Electrical (Circuit Branch Only) Stipend INR = 50000 /- per month PPO will be offered on a performance basis Roles Offered TSA - Technical Sales Associate FAE - Field Applications Engineer Location Bangalore/Pune/Delhi Do Note their India Head Office is in Bangalore, with a larger number employees/interns working out of the Bangalore Office. Pre-Placement Talk (PPT) - 27th July, 2023 Essential - To attend The Pre-Placement Talk of TI was conducted in Online Mode on 27th July, 2023 around 5:00pm. The Talk included the HR Team as well as a few senior representatives from TI. It began with the description of TI, its products, its businesses, impact, global presence, local presence in India, revenue and other details about the company. Followed by which there was a discussion on the employee statistics, work culture, growth trajectory as well as TI’s push towards research. Post the same, there was a description of the Job Profile being offered to students at VJTI - FAE (Field Applications Engineer) and TSA (Technical Sales Associate), what will be the quality and type of work being conducted, and what’s expected from an employee working in the aforementioned roles. The Full-Time CTC was also discussed in brief for both the roles. There was also a description of the Training and opportunities provided to Freshers. Post the description of Full-Time offering, there was a description of the internship programme also. There was also a description of the Growth Trajectory as an employee. The Panel was also open to questions at the end, and a few key questions were answered particularly on the tips for prep for assessment and interviews. I would highly recommend one to attend the Pre-Placement Talk as one can understand the business of the company, as well as what’s expected of an employee in the specific role. As well as getting some insights on the assessments, Interview, as well as overall compensation and role. It’s also a good opportunity to ask questions to senior representatives of the company, say regarding growth or other technical aspects of a role. Take down important information/points and it will be helpful to answer crucial questions about the company during the Interview Process particularly during the HR Rounds. You could also take screenshots of the PPT as it contains info about the company's values, reach, goals, employee commitments/benefits, internship program details, full-time internship offering and much more. Online Technical Assessment - 31st August, 2023 Solve Very Well We had to register for the Online Technical Assessment a few days prior to the Test. There was an option to select whether we were interested in FAE/TSA/Both. I will highly recommend to select both if you are unsure. Online Assessment was on 31st August, 2023 at 6:00pm. With 2 sections (both timed separately) a. Technical Based Questions (20 Questions) 45 Minutes - Questions were based on core concepts of Analog and Digital Electronics, Microprocessors, Core Circuital Concepts. Particular focus on Amplifiers, Filters, RLC Circuits, core circuital concepts. b. Aptitude Based Question (20 Questions) 30 Minutes - Questions were mainly aptitude based. With a focus on problem solving, logical reasoning, puzzles, comprehensions, data analysis and quantitative reasoning. Do note, there was negative marking for both the sections +1/-0.25, hence it recommended to answer with caution. Also keep track of the time during both the sections. Don’t waste too much time on a particular question, as some questions were designed that way. Give the test in a quiet environment without any external distractions/disturbances, with good internet connectivity, and interrupted power. Be ready a few minutes prior to the starting time of the test, so you have sufficient time for unforeseen delays, so you can login on Time. Prepare the Technical section well. Sleep Well, don’t stay hungry, Stay Hydrated, Be Calm and give your best, during the test. Interview Round 1 - 5th September, 2023 Think and patiently answer Total 22 Students were shortlisted for the interviews, 11 each in TSA and FAE. Interviews were conducted offline in-person in TPO, 9am onwards. Panelists for both roles were different. There was 1 interviewer for my 1st round. It was a combination of Technical + Sales Interview. I was asked to give a brief introduction, followed by a description of my current/ongoing work/projects. There were a few cross-questions on the same. I was given a hypothetical situation on how and using what steps would I utilize TI’s historic Sales data, say of the past 5-10 years for analysis. There were follow-up questions on the same regarding methodologies, trends to be found, cases given. Now the interviewer asked a few technical questions, for about 10-15 minutes. To make a few Circuits, graphs of output, describe the working and outputs of certain electronic devices/circuits. He did try to confuse me in the process, and tried to imply that what I’d answered was wrong. But stay confident with your answer, don’t budge and don’t get scared (yeah, he did scare a hell lot of me). Now a few questions were asked about my JEE journey, why VJTI, why Electronics Engineering, and my overall experience. He was not very happy with my long answers, so he clearly pointed out and stated that he is not satisfied with my answers, they’re too long, sometimes going out of context and not on point. He specified that from now on I need to answer well. Then why TI, why the TSA role. Furthermore a few questions were asked according to my resume, particularly on my project experience, cross-questions on my projects, and my work in technical/cultural committee’s in VJTI. He did go into some details well like on my work in e-Yantra, which sensors used, which microcontroller, and on software. He also asked if I could show some working demo - which I did. He also asked if I could scale any of those projects, is it viable as a business, at what stage is it (prototyping/production). He also asked if I was aware about similar tech in industry, or showcased in recent tech/business/product summits. And a few more questions continued. As my interview was the last in the TSA role, my interviewer was constantly comparing my resume with a few of my classmates. Also asking a few questions about the difference between my contribution and one of my classmates in a competition. I answered in good spirit, explaining the different nature of both our themes, and explaining the difference of work done by him and me, and the difference in tech stack utilized. Now, came the main marketing/sales scenario, wherein he said that we will do a roleplay. Wherein I was a TI sales executive, and the interviewer was an angry customer, who had ordered well in advance, and due to some production and supply chain issues in the entire industry (not company specific), the client’s delivery completion will be delayed by 6 months. And the client is very upset and angry. So, I first asked a few questions to get more details about the situation, before starting the roleplay. About the client, about TI, what will TI be able to fulfill, so I can do a negotiation. I would highly recommend you get more context of the entire situation, and ask what assumptions you can make. As it will be useful information that can be utilized. The interviewer behaved like a very angry and stubborn client, giving clear threats of leaving TI, of competitors supplying on time, of its commitments to its customers. Demanding TI give it priority and supply the entire order then and there, as TI had the capacity by not supplying to other clients of TI. He was not willing to listen to any argument. So I also had to be patient, to explain to him the entire problem with very angry/sharp questions and remarks. Post some discussion, the client then again started arguing on the same terms as initially, and I had to again explain peacefully. Now there was demand for Loss Compensation, and other commitments from TI. Wherein I had to make sound decisions so TI is not at a loss, and at the receiving end. At the end, with dialogue and discussion, we came to a reasonable conclusion. This discussion lasted for at least 20 minutes, and the interviewer was happy that I did not give up, and explained the industry and supply chain problem patiently to the client, and tried to come to a settlement with discussion. During the entire interview, he repeatedly asked why I was preferring the TSA role and not the FAE role, as my academic background was very sound and I’d done work particularly in robotics and technical domain. I clearly explained a few reasons. I would recommend you be firm/confident on your decision/choice and not budge. Also, he advised me on my delivery of answering questions in the interview. Few mistakes I made in this regard. He again specified that I need to learn to answer in brief and short, to the point. Now if you have been shortlisted for TSA, you have the choice to switch to the FAE role also, and continue your interview for the FAE role. As in the case of Lakshya, who was shortlisted for TSA, but was more inclined towards the FAE role. So you could describe if you’re inclined towards the FAE role in the 1st round itself, and again be firm on your decision. Entire 1st round lasted for about 50 mins to 1 hour. Interview Round 2 - 5th September, 2023 Think and Patiently answer, with confidence Total 7 Students were shortlisted for the 2nd round of interview, 4 in TSA and 3 in FAE. Interviews were conducted offline in-person in TPO, 2:30pm onwards. Panelists for both roles were different. There were 2 interviewers for my 2nd round. It was a combination of Technical + Sales + HR/Behavioural Again I was asked for my introduction as a short description on my previous and ongoing projects. A few cross questions were asked on the same. Followed by a few detailed questions according to my resume on my previous projects and experience and contribution in cultural and technical clubs in college. There were a few cross questions with a few sharp on-point questions requiring sharp answers. A few technical questions were also asked. A few of my batchmates were asked several technical questions, as well as marketing/sales scenarios depending on what was asked in the 1st round. Now I was asked about why TI, why TSA role particularly. There were a few cross-questions even asking why I was not opting for FAE due to my academic background and experience in robotics and technical projects. Again, be confident about your decision and explain properly. Now I was asked if I was interested in Business, or Entrepreneurship in the short term or long term, with proper reasons expected. A few cross questions also. Now I was asked if I was following current affairs, and was asked what’s hot news in the Finance world, and what’s my opinion of economic or government policies and asked for an example. Now I was asked if I was aware about PLI (Production Linked Incentive Scheme). I was asked how it would be beneficial for a company like TI. I was asked what the role of PLI is in supply chain, investments for growth in India for local home-grown companies and international MNCs. Does it aid the growth of local companies and international MNCs, and how? All of these questions expected detailed answers with reasons, and a few cross questions followed. There was a particular question on Supply Chain in general. And a few questions were asked about what's the problem with PLI in India, and my opinion on India scaling manufacturing. They also asked for my opinion on the semiconductor industry in India, how to I expect its growth and how TI would play a role in the same, and how could TI grow. A few questions were asked on semiconductor manufacturing, and in general bringing new technology to India, and research potential and growth in India. There were many cross-questions regarding the same. Now I was asked about my plans for my Masters. I would like to clearly recommend that you do describe the same well. Both the interviewers asked a few cross questions regarding my reasons for the same. Then I was asked whether I would be willing to join TI if I was offered a PPO. Few cross-questions for the same. Now I was asked if I would be willing to sign a bond for 4 years with TI if I was offered a PPO. A lot of cross-questions for the same. Then one of the interviewers explained how he still came back to TI post doing an Executive Masters course, and stated that work experience in TI would add value to my profile. And the same question was asked again. With a discussion following the same. This was discussed for about 10 minutes, do answer this part well. Maybe prepare for such questions in any interview, as your answers will be crucial for your success, as your plans should be at least partially aligned with that of the company at hand. Post the same, I was asked about my other interests, and a few cross questions on the same. I was also asked about my family background. Particularly the education and current work of my parents. And why I was interested in the Sales/Marketing role even though I’m in Engineering with a sound technical background. This concluded the interview, and the interviewers were open to questions. I asked for their feedback. And a few questions on the growth trajectory at TI. I would highly recommend you ask questions, as it shows your interest in the company and the role. Entire 2nd round lasted for about 50 mins to 1 hour. The result was announced around 9pm on 5th September, 2023. And I was successfully selected for the TSA Intern Role. 2 of my batchmates were also selected for the FAE Intern Role. Tips Work Hard, Prepare Well, Answer with confidence a. I would highly recommend you revise your basics and core concepts of Analog and Digital Electronics, Circuits, Microprocessors. As well as go into depth in these subjects, particularly for the FAE role, but this part is still important for the TSA role also. b. For the TSA role, look up/refer to business case studies, marketing/sales material. Even prepare well for aptitude assessment. c. For TI, look up the various products sold by TI, different segments, and TI’s presence in those segments. Maybe if available, look up statistics published by the company. d. Always think well before answering. Don’t haste through, think well, and use your words wisely. e. Be mentally and physically prepared for long, sharp interviews. Do not lose your ground, answer with confidence. Stay hydrated at all times, Sleep well and don’t go hungry before the Online Assessment or Interview. f. Read well regarding the company, what it does, what’s in for you, how you can contribute, what’s job profile/work. g. Make a good resume!!! I can’t emphasize enough. All details written in a sharp but neat package. All important information, key details to be mentioned clearly. Use small sentences and important keywords to describe yourself and your experience/projects. It’s recommended to display academic background also. h. Be well versed with every minute detail of your Resume. Think of what cross-questions or further details can be asked from what’s mentioned. Be prepared for everything. i. Ask seniors for advice on interviews from their past experience, read about interview experiences online/TPO provided. As it will help you get mentally prepared for the same. j. Before the interviews, if there is a sheet sent via mail which specifies your interview time and interviewer name (not always provided). Take advantage of this.I would check their Linkedin profiles and the role and the work they do. This gives an insight on what you should focus more on. k. Look up regarding the company's Senior Management, short term and long term goals, and what would be impacted by your profile. l. This link contains the JD and preparation material as provided to us by TI in the initial communication post the PPT, before the Online Assessment. Utilize the same well. All the Best !!! Trust the process :)
